reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that tennis point outcomes are determined by a sequence of spatiotemporally aligned strategic decisions. Each shot contributes to a cumulative dominance score D(t), evolving through time. Style priors P_i encode individual tactical preferences, while context priors C_rally modulate these preferences dynamically. The interplay between these elements forms a probabilistic model where P_i and C_rally jointly influence the likelihood of a point outcome. The failure mode occurs when either style priors are misapplied due to opponent novelty or context priors fail to capture emergent rally dynamics. These primitives enable a dual framework: one for modeling dominant patterns (style) and another for adapting to situational constraints (context).
